Hi Alexandra,

Congrats again on completing the contract — glad to have HelixCare onboard. Attached is a working draft of the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that embeds the post-signature implementation steps: rollout windows, canary gating, migration cutover, and the initial training curriculum. Key highlights: 

- 6-week execution window from go-live signature to first production traffic shift
- Canary exercise during week 3 with a 48h observation and rollback window
- Two migration windows (pilot -> broad) planned during low-traffic nights
- Training: 3 instructor-led sessions + on-demand skill-transfer docs for ops and devs

Please review the attached MAP and the evaluation criteria spreadsheet. Items we need to lock down this week: final canary date, primary migration window, and your acceptance criteria for the staging run.

Attachments: MAP_HelixCare_20270925.pdf, evaluation_criteria_helix.xlsx

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm preferred canary week (target: Oct 11-17)
2) We finalize the runbook and sign off on rollback gates (internal)
3) Procurement and SSO integrations mapped by your DevOps

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if helpful.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Director, Customer Success

- New canary target: week of Oct 4 (pilot traffic window Oct 6-7) 
- Canary scope: 5% production traffic routed to Redwood, 2-hour rolling ramp, automated rollback on error rate > 3x baseline or latency spike > 2x p50
- Training schedule: Week of Oct 11 we run 3 x 90-min instructor sessions (Ops Deep Dive, Runbook Walkthrough, Incident Response Playbook) and drop recordings to the shared Drive
- Migration windows: Oct 14-16 night window (broad migration), secondary fallback nights Oct 21-23

Thanks team — quick technical checklist from my side to ensure the canary is actionable:

- Pin model version to v1.2.0-quant for the canary and record the backend variant id in the runbook
- KV cache priming: schedule synthetic warmup 1 hour before canary start to avoid cold-start penalties
- Observability: wire the per-route tracing hook and token-level cost sampling for the 48h post-canary window
- Acceptance criteria (pass if all true): error rate <= 1.5x baseline, p95 latency within 1.3x baseline, no unrecoverable stateful errors for 48h

Attaching model-variants.yml for the customer-facing note so they can see what we will pin. Also recommend we add a short line in the MAP about fallback to smaller model variant if memory OOM occurs during the canary.

Jonas Weber
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
